verdict.line: You lose short trades and any all-in before level 6, but you close the gap once Blade of the Ruined King and full stacks come online around level 9-11.

brief.thesis: Sett punishes exactly the short trades Irelia's kit wants to throw: Haymaker banks free damage off every poke and pays it back as a shielded true-damage burst, and Facebreaker turns a careless step onto the wave into a stun instead of a slow. The 44.6% win rate over 707 games and Sett's lane and solo-kill advantage both come from Irelia over-committing early rather than a hard mechanical counter - this is a patience matchup, not a lost one.

theirWindow.when: you're melee near minions, his cooldowns are up
theirWindow.what: Back off the wave immediately. Facebreaker (E, 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s cd, range 490) stuns if it catches you between two sides but only slows if you're alone on one side, so staying off the minions turns his all-in tool into a non-event.

yourWindow.when: Sett's Q, W, and E are all on cooldown
yourWindow.what: Engage with Q (Bladesurge, 10/9/8/7/6s cd) into E (Flawless Duet, 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s cd) for the stun and Mark, then dash again off the Mark to refresh Q and keep swinging.

start.why: The 86.3% pick rate reflects how often you need the extra sustain to outlast Sett's regen-heavy passive and Haymaker's true-damage punch across level 1-5 trades.

boots.why: Cuts down the alternating auto-attack chip damage from his Pit Grit passive and the on-hit portion of Knuckle Down, which is what actually wins him short trades.

core.why: Max-health damage and the on-hit heal directly offset the sustain gap Sett's passive regen creates, and it's the highest-picked first item at 25.8%/21.5% across both winning paths.
Rewards the split-push and dueling angle you're forced into after losing early lane priority, and pairs with BORK for consistent DPS in extended fights.
The 55.5% win-rate path over 119 games - the damage-over-time conversion smooths out Haymaker's burst true damage specifically.

you're ahead on gold and want to end the game faster instead of grinding out extended duels

runes.keystoneWhy: The adaptive force ramp and healing from stacking Conqueror across a longer trade window is what closes the sustain gap against Sett's Pit Grit regen and Haymaker burst.

summoners.why: The 77.1% pick rate makes sense here - Ignite directly cuts into Sett's missing-health regen from Pit Grit, which is otherwise what lets him win extended lane trades against you.

playing.title: Track his Grit before trading
playing.detail: Haymaker passively stores damage Sett takes as Grit; if you've been meleeing him for several autos or a full Q-E combo, expect a shielded true-damage punch back and don't stand in it.

playing.title: Stay off the minion wave
playing.detail: Facebreaker only stuns if it catches you between two sides - staying clear of the wave means any E that reaches you is just a slow, not a lockdown into a full combo.

playing.title: Punish only empty cooldowns
playing.detail: Wait until Sett's Q, W, and E are all visibly down before committing your Q-E all-in; going in while any of them are up is how you feed his solo-kill advantage.

playing.title: Bank four passive stacks first
playing.detail: Hold the all-in until Ionian Fervor is at max stacks so you get the attack speed and bonus on-hit damage before you commit, per the matchup's own read on engaging aggressively.

playing.title: Charge W to shrug off pokes
playing.detail: Defiant Dance reduces physical damage taken while charging, so use it to eat his empowered right-hand punch during a trade instead of trying to out-trade it with autos.

playing.title: Respect level 6 all-ins
playing.detail: The Show Stopper (125/105/85/0/0s becomes 120/100/80/80/80s for Sett) can carry you toward his jungler or tower - don't shove past minion support once he hits 6.

playing.title: Rush BORK before fighting for tempo
playing.detail: Blade of the Ruined King's health-scaling damage and heal are the single biggest lever for flipping this matchup from level 9 onward, so prioritize completing it over side items.

brief.patchCaveat: The build order, win rates, and item/rune pick rates are pulled directly from measured games on the current patch via OP.GG; the mechanical reasoning - cooldown windows, stack timing, and trade patterns - is my own read of the two kits.
